issues.reason: 'According to <source>, P' attributes P without committing the speaker to it, so asserting the introduce event with (Future sk_introduce_1) at top level asserts more than the text states — exactly the flattening the Impersonal reported attitudes section forbids ('it does not make P true, so P must never be flattened into top-level facts').

gaps_confirmed: evidential attribution 'According to <source>, P': no licensed carrier scopes or hedges the reported proposition — the impersonal-reported-attitude route needs a matrix attitude verb, which a PP evidential does not supply
pre-nominal office title on a proper name ('Florida Speaker Johnnie Byrd'): the title rule names only kinship/courtesy titles, so the stated office survives only inside the Name string
new_gaps: AccordingTo has no licensed argument shape as a seal-bearer: the preposition-named oblique is defined as (<Prep> <event> <object>), so putting a sealed (And …) in its first slot is improvised — the repair uses it because the licensed alternative would be to delete the sentence's entire content

whether a definite referent's identifying but non-typing atoms project out of a seal ('the special session Monday' — (Time sk_session_1 (Weekday monday))): the projection rule names only Member/Name typing atoms
repair_summary: Sealed the reported proposition (the introduce event class, Agent, Theme, Future and During atoms) as the first argument of the already-present AccordingTo atom instead of asserting it at top level; kept every definite/named referent's typing atom at top level per the seal-projection rule, and left all other atoms and their order unchanged.
